PullRequest.Title: agentHost: stop injecting the artifact tools reminder
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #338589

The artifact tools reminder was added to the first user message of every chat, so it was re-sent with every model request. The always-loaded `add_artifact_or_reference` tool description already carries the same guidance, so this removes `ArtifactToolsContribution` and `ARTIFACT_TOOLS_INSTRUCTION`.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A long artifact reminder duplicated guidance already present in an always-loaded tool definition and was embedded in the first user prompt, causing that text to remain in the conversation context processed by subsequent model requests for the chat.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Repeated model-input bytes/tokens and associated provider processing/user cost for artifact-enabled chats.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The PR deletes ARTIFACT_TOOLS_INSTRUCTION and unregisters/deletes ArtifactToolsContribution, so new chats no longer append the duplicate reminder to their first model-visible prompt; the non-deferred add_artifact_or_reference tool description remains available with the required guidance.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, ArtifactToolsContribution.onOutgoingTurn returned ARTIFACT_TOOLS_INSTRUCTION on each chat's first outgoing turn; AgentSideEffects forwarded contribution instructions as hostInstructions into agent.chats.sendMessage. Copilot injects these as user-prompt additionalContext, Claude via getUserPromptAdditionalContext, and Codex via turn/start additionalContext, placing the long reminder into model context. The add_artifact_or_reference definition is deferLoading:false and already contains the same classification, batching, optional-registration, and exclusion guidance, so the separate reminder duplicated always-loaded tool text. The deleted base line 276 is the long duplicate prompt, and blame resolves it to b0dad94048b3b988c8aa325a46ce7998f2abe0bb.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start and continue an artifact-enabled chat through Copilot, Claude, or Codex
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each accepted turn runs outgoing contributions, forwards hostInstructions through AgentSideEffects, then crosses the provider send boundary before model work can begin. Before the PR, the first turn also embedded the long artifact reminder in model context; after the PR, only the already-advertised non-deferred tool definition carries that guidance.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the user turn and host additional context to the provider runtime/model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider send per accepted user turn; the provider may make multiple model requests during an agentic turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The first outgoing turn of each fresh artifact-enabled chat included ARTIFACT_TOOLS_INSTRUCTION in addition to the non-deferred add_artifact_or_reference tool description; later sends omitted a new instruction, but the first prompt remained part of conversation context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The send is on the turn critical path. The PR reduces its first-turn context and the context retained for later model requests but does not remove or add the boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scaled with the number of fresh chats and with downstream model requests that processed the conversation containing the duplicated first-turn text.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Turns are sequenced per chat/provider session. One host send occurs per accepted turn; an agentic turn may perform multiple downstream model requests, all against the conversation containing the first prompt context.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The contribution used a per-chat memento as a one-shot guard, including negative handling for restored non-empty chats. The PR removes that memento and duplicate prompt text. The non-deferred add tool definition remains always loaded; provider prompt caches can now operate on a smaller prompt without this redundant context.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted contribution returned the constant, AgentSideEffects forwarded it as hostInstructions, and all three providers inject hostInstructions into model-visible additional context.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact token count, cache pricing, and number of downstream model requests vary by provider and task, but the duplicated context and provider-boundary reachability are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression introduced. This is a concrete repeated-prompt-work fix and was recorded with report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a chat with existing turns, then send another turn
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hydration completes before restored turns are exposed. Before the PR, ArtifactToolsContribution only set a per-chat memento for a non-empty restored history; it performed no filesystem, IPC, subprocess, or network operation. The subsequent provider send already omitted artifact guidance, so the PR does not alter its boundary payload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the next restored-chat turn to the provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hydration marked firstTurnSeen and the next turn sent no artifact reminder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider send remains critical, but its payload is unchanged for non-empty restored chats because the old hydration hook suppressed the artifact reminder.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of restored chats and restored turns; the deleted hook was O(1) per hydrated chat and did not scan turn contents.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hydration stages run in contribution order for one chat. Provider turns remain sequenced per chat.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Before the PR, a chat-scoped memento survived until chat disposal; after the PR, that small entry no longer exists. Provider cache behavior for restored non-empty chats is otherwise unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted onHydrateTurns checked only turns.length and set one memento.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The removed memento has negligible per-chat size; no material performance regression is plausible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the change removes small CPU/allocation work.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tool definitions are advertised to provider sessions; actual add/remove/list execution occurs only after a model tool call. The PR removes only a separate instruction constant and leaves tool definitions, execution, persistence, and pull-request association paths unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize artifact tool definitions into provider-visible tool metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One non-deferred add-tool definition plus deferred list/remove definitions per enabled session/provider prompt configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same tool definitions were advertised, while the first turn additionally duplicated much of the add-tool guidance through ARTIFACT_TOOLS_INSTRUCTION.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The add tool description remains model-visible and carries the required guidance; the PR does not increase definition count or size.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist artifacts and optionally associate GitHub pull requests after an actual tool invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One persistence mutation per tool call; GitHub association is batched for URLs when the batch accessor exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the ordinary chat-send path unless the model invokes the artifact tool; entirely unchanged by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of enabled sessions, artifact tool calls, and batched artifact/PR entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Advertisement is grouped per session. Add batches related artifact entries in one call; any persistence or GitHub association behavior is unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The add tool remains deferLoading:false, so its description is available without discovery; list/remove remain deferred. No cache key, invalidation, or coalescing behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from unchanged definitions and execution body around the deleted constant.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific serialization and tool-schema caching are opaque, but unchanged; only the duplicate reminder is removed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; required guidance remains in the existing non-deferred definition and no execution boundary was added.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all six changed files and all diff pages. No diff-introduced performance findings were found. The runtime change removes duplicated model-context work and a small per-chat memento; the concrete historical regression fix was recorded against the blamed base line.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
